title: Evidgate permission catalogue
description: Shape of contracts/permissions.json (00 §2, 02 D2). Deliberately NOT under contracts/schemas/, contracts/adapter/ or contracts/manifest/: both runtime schema loaders compile every *.json under those three roots, and this schema describes a build-time catalogue rather than a request body. Validated by tests/Contract.Tests/PermissionCatalogueTests.cs; the cross-field rules a JSON Schema cannot express (code == resource:action, role permissions ⊆ catalogue, the reserved/assignable invariants) are asserted there too.

version.description: Catalogue format version; a breaking change bumps this and the C# constants' namespace-free contract stays.

comment.description: Human note on how the file is consumed; never machine-read.

roles.description: The 00 §2 built-in roles and their permission sets — the seed source of public.role / public.role_permission.

permissions.description: Every resource:action string any plan uses — the seed source of public.permission.

token_denied.description: The codes an API token can never hold: an automation token is denied every administrative permission. Entries are exact codes or `resource:*` wildcards, expanded against `permissions` by scripts/generate-permissions.py (an entry that matches no code fails generation, so a typo cannot silently widen a token), and the expansion must equal the `admin`-flagged codes — tests/Contract.Tests asserts both directions.

code.description: Permission code shape of 00 §2: resource:action, lower_snake on both sides (the same regex as PermissionAttribute).

roleCode.description: Role code shape (00 §2 role codes, snake_case).

kind.description: Principal class the role is for: member = a human member of an org (T79's member principal), service = a CI/agent service identity, staff = Evidgate personnel.

permissions.description: Permission codes granted by this role; each must exist in `permissions[]`.

resource.description: The code's resource half (the text before ':').

action.description: The code's action half (the text after ':').

sensitive.description: True when the permission gates secret-adjacent data or returns a plaintext secret once; AC5 asserts no unprivileged role holds one.

reserved.description: True when the string is catalogue-only today: its first consumer is a V2/V3 story, so no V1 endpoint or handler references it yet (AC2's 'referenced or reserved' rule).

tenant_assignable.description: False for a code a member principal must never hold (support:*, billing:*, agent-only, T79): a custom role containing one is 422 permission_not_assignable and the evaluator filters them out of a member's grant set.

admin.description: True for an administrative code — membership and role management, tenant-wide settings, secrets, policy, audit and security reads. An automation token is denied every one of them: the `token_denied` expansion must equal the set flagged here, so adding an administrative code without denying it to tokens fails the contract tests.
